PERSONAL WINDOWS ARM64 BUILD

This setup builds official Nextcloud Desktop v35.0.2 with ARM64 fixes to its
build tools. Application and packaging sources outside .github remain identical
to official commit 07761410a90a2f27007932fcb61afc23ddda5998.

FEATURES AND LIMITS

No feature-removal patch is applied. The normal Windows build targets, including
virtual files, remain in the source. Keeping them does not prove that installation,
Explorer registration, virtual files, or syncing work on a physical ARM64 device.
The generic Craft NSIS installer must be tested for these behaviors. It is an
unsigned personal build. Its installer launcher may use a different architecture
from the ARM64 application payload.

HOW TO START

1. Push the prepared windows-arm64 branch to lzs/nextcloud-desktop.
2. Visit https://github.com/lzs/nextcloud-desktop/actions and enable Actions if
   GitHub asks. If Actions was disabled when you pushed, enable it and use the
   default-branch option below to start the build manually.
3. The first push adding the workflow starts Build Windows ARM64. Open the run
   to follow its progress. Changes to its scripts or pins start another build.
4. On success, download nextcloud-windows-arm64-35.0.2 from the run's Artifacts
   section. Extract it to find the installer, checksum, build manifest, generated
   Craft configuration, and exact patches applied to the upstream build tools.

Enable Actions BEFORE the first push for the simplest setup. No GitHub token or
code-signing certificate needs to be added as a secret. The workflow's repository
token has read-only contents access and cannot publish releases or push code.

If you want a Run workflow button, set windows-arm64 as your fork's default
branch in Settings > General > Default branch. GitHub requires workflow_dispatch
to be present on the default branch. This optional change does not affect upstream.

TIME AND RESTARTS

The first build compiles dependencies, including Qt, and can take hours. The
hosted job has a six-hour limit. Six checkpoints save completed dependency phases
in YOUR repository's Actions cache. Re-run a failed job to reuse matching completed
phases. A phase interrupted before completion may need to rebuild. These caches
are not fetched from the reference project. Changing pins/scripts/workflow changes
the cache fingerprint and starts with matching inputs only. Delete your own cache
in Actions > Caches when you want a completely fresh dependency build.

If a build fails, open its first failing step. The workflow also attempts to
save craft-client.log, craft-package.log, and test diagnostic logs on failure.
Dependency failures are visible in the job log. A failed test prevents packaging;
the setup does not label a failing build as successful.

SOURCE AND TRUST

.github/arm64-pins.json records exact official commits for the application, Craft,
CraftMaster, and KDE/Nextcloud dependency recipes. The build checks the application
source against the pinned official release and downloads build tools directly from
their listed upstream repositories. It disables Craft's precompiled dependency
cache. Compilers, GitHub Actions, binary build utilities, Python packages, and
Microsoft runtime files remain external build inputs. Dependency recipes may
fetch those inputs and sources from their own upstream URLs. This is not a claim
of a hermetic or bit-for-bit reproducible build.

The ARM64 build scripts and tests were adapted from:
https://github.com/Dudiebug/nextclouddesktoparm
arm64-tooling commit d8634255ce3a671629424e1a5cabdd7e962e1ad8

Their copyright and GPL-2.0-or-later notices are retained. The scripts are included
in YOUR repository, where they can be read and changed. The build never downloads
that project's scripts, releases, or dependency caches at runtime. Building from
source does not remove the need to review copied build instructions.

Adaptations include fixed official source/tool revisions, source verification,
local patch manifests, read-only repository permissions, no release publishing,
strict matching cache keys, and expanded ARM64 binary verification. An obsolete
resource-header rewriting patch was removed; the resource wrapper invokes the
Windows SDK resource compiler and ARM64 cvtres instead. Test environment changes
use UTC and the Windows Vista widget style for widget tests, with Qt Quick tests
run separately; test sources and their pass/fail results are retained.

The workflow is AI-assisted. Any later upstream contribution must follow
Nextcloud's contribution and AI policies, including human review, testing,
authorship disclosure, and human-written project communication.

LOCAL VALIDATION ON 2026-10-31

69 build-script tests passed. ARM64 patches applied successfully to the exact
pinned Craft and dependency-recipe sources. Patched Python syntax was checked.
Workflow YAML and its embedded PowerShell scripts were checked locally.
The complete ARM64 compile, client tests, installer, and physical-device behavior
have not been validated locally. The first Actions run is required to establish
whether the complete build succeeds.
